paper.task: Takes an unordered set of points from a Euclidean space (a point cloud) and outputs either a category for the whole point cloud (classification) or per-point quantities such as segmentation labels (segmentation).

components.name: input points
components.what: the input point set {x1, ..., xn}: an unordered subset of points from a Euclidean space

provenance.quote: Our input is a subset of points from an Euclidean space.

components.name: T-net
components.what: joint alignment mini-network that predicts an affine transformation matrix for the input points

provenance.quote: We predict an affine transformation matrix by a mini-network (T-net in Fig 2)

components.name: point independent feature extraction
components.what: per-point feature extraction inside the T-net

provenance.quote: The mini-network itself resembles the big network and is composed by basic modules of point independent feature extraction

components.name: max pooling
components.what: max pooling inside the T-net

provenance.quote: composed by basic modules of point independent feature extraction, max pooling and fully connected layers

components.name: fully connected layers
components.what: fully connected layers inside the T-net

provenance.quote: point independent feature extraction, max pooling and fully connected layers

components.name: apply transformation
components.what: the predicted affine transformation is applied directly to the coordinates of the input points, aligning them to a canonical space

provenance.quote: directly apply this transformation to the coordinates of input points

components.name: basic module
components.what: the symmetric-function module f({x1..xn}) ~ g(h(x1), ..., h(xn)): h applied to every point, then a symmetric g

provenance.quote: our basic module is very simple: we approximate h by a multi-layer perceptron network and g by a composition of a single variable function and a max pooling function

components.name: multi-layer perceptron network
components.what: approximates h: R^N -> R^K, applied to each point x_i separately to give per-point features h(x_i)

provenance.quote: we approximate h by a multi-layer perceptron network

components.name: max pooling layer
components.what: MAX: the symmetric function that aggregates the n per-point vectors into one vector of element-wise maxima (dimension K, the bottleneck dimension)

provenance.quote: the max pooling layer as a symmetric function to aggregate information from all the points

components.name: single variable function
components.what: gamma, the continuous function applied after max pooling so that g = gamma o MAX

provenance.quote: g by a composition of a single variable function and a max pooling function

components.name: global feature
components.what: the vector [f1, ..., fK]: a global signature of the input set

provenance.quote: The output from the above section forms a vector [f 1 , . . . , f K ], which is a global signature of the input set.

components.name: SVM or multi-layer perceptron classifier
components.what: classifier trained on the global feature for shape classification

provenance.quote: We can easily train a SVM or multi-layer perceptron classifier on the shape global features for classification.

components.name: classification scores
components.what: output of the classification network: the point cloud category

provenance.quote: such as classification or segmentation scores

components.name: local and global information combination structure
components.what: the segmentation network's addition: the global feature is fed back to the per-point features and new per-point features are extracted

provenance.quote: a local and global information combination structure

components.name: concatenation
components.what: the global feature is concatenated with each of the point features

provenance.quote: we feed it back to per point features by concatenating the global feature with each of the point features

components.name: per point feature extraction
components.what: extracts new per-point features from the combined point features (layer type not stated)

provenance.quote: Then we extract new per point features based on the combined point features

components.name: segmentation scores
components.what: per-point quantities predicted by the segmentation network (e.g. part or scene segmentation labels; the text also mentions per-point normals)

provenance.quote: our network is able to predict per point quantities that rely on both local geometry and global semantics

components.name: feature alignment network
components.what: a second joint alignment mini-network inserted on point features; predicts the feature transformation matrix A

provenance.quote: We can insert another alignment network on point features and predict a feature transformation matrix

components.name: align features
components.what: the feature transformation matrix A is applied to the point features to align features from different input point clouds

provenance.quote: predict a feature transformation matrix to align features from different input point clouds

components.name: L reg
components.what: regularization term ||I - A A^T||_F^2 that constrains the feature transformation matrix A to be close to orthogonal

provenance.quote: We constrain the feature transformation matrix to be close to orthogonal matrix

components.name: softmax training loss
components.what: the network's training loss, to which L_reg is added

provenance.quote: We therefore add a regularization term to our softmax training loss.

unclear: What the input T-net takes as input is not stated. The text says it predicts an affine matrix that is applied to the input points and that it 'resembles the big network' with 'point independent feature extraction', which suggests it reads the input points, but no input flow is stated, so none is recorded.

The T-net is listed as 'point independent feature extraction, max pooling and fully connected layers'; that is a description order, not a stated flow, so no flow is recorded between these parts. The text defers T-net details to the supplementary.
Whether the feature alignment network has the same composition as the input T-net is not stated (only 'predicted by a mini-network').

Where the feature alignment network is inserted (on which point features of h, e.g. between layers of the MLP or after it) and where the aligned features go next are not stated; the 'align features' op therefore has no recorded output.
Which point features are concatenated with the global feature in segmentation (from which layer, and whether before or after feature alignment) is not stated.
How the new per-point features are extracted after concatenation (layer type and widths) and how the per-point quantities are predicted from them are not stated.

The text says g is a composition of a single variable function γ and max pooling, and that the section's output is the vector [f1, ..., fK]; it also calls K the dimension of the max pooling layer. Whether γ is a separate drawn layer, and whether the global feature is taken after max pooling or after γ, is not stated.
Which outputs the softmax training loss is computed on (classification scores, segmentation scores or both) and with which labels is not stated, so the softmax loss has only L_reg recorded as input.

The classification and segmentation networks 'share a great portion of structures', but which parts are shared is not stated; the text refers to the Fig 2 caption for the pipeline, which is not available in this blind run.
The classifier is described as 'a SVM or multi-layer perceptron classifier'; which one the network uses is not fixed by the text.

No layer widths, number of points or matrix sizes are given (no numbers for K, N or n); notation is also inconsistent: Sec. 4.1 says 'N 3D point sets' / 'N ! permutations' (N = number of points) while Eq. (1) uses n points in R^N.
Eq. (1)'s domain/codomain line is garbled in the extraction (split superscripts and an under-brace 'n'); read as f: 2^(R^N) -> R, h: R^N -> R^K, g: R^K x ... x R^K (n times) -> R symmetric.
The max pooling layer is a standard layer; it is marked proposed only because the text lists 'the max pooling layer as a symmetric function' among the network's three key modules.

The T-net builds on the spatial transformer idea of Jaderberg et al. [9]; it is marked proposed because the joint alignment networks are listed among the three key modules and the text contrasts its simpler design with [9].
Sec. 4.3 is interrupted by Table 1 text (ModelNet40 classification results) and Theorem 2 appears cut off after part (b); this is extraction noise and was not used.
